newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand eliminates net foreign currency debt.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand eliminates net foreign currency debt.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch said New Zealand's net public foreign currency debt would be eliminated on Friday after the government paid the final US$1.092 billion in New York.
Birch said the payment to the government from Fletcher Challenge Ltd for the purchase of state-owned Forestry Corporation would eliminate the last NZ$1.6 billion.

The government's net public debt in both foreign and local currency was NZ$28.64 billion in the year ended June 1996, according to figures released in the Treasury's pre-election economic and fiscal update.
Gross public debt was $41.5 billion while financial assets totalled $12.86 billion.
Birch said net public foreign currency debt had fallen from $15.9 billion in 1990 to nil.
Total net public debt was $11,109 for every New Zealander in 1991/92. It was $6,200 this financial year and was forecast to fall to $3,763 by 1999/2000.
Birch said the remaining debt was denominated in New Zealand dollars and the government was committed to paying that back too. --Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
